Branch: `claude/issue-6240-object-payload-fields-map`

Serial constraints — file face, located on `origin/main` **after** #6238 landed: `packages/app-shell/src/services/MetadataService.ts` — `saveObject` / `toObjectPayload` at `:275-277`, `saveFields` at `:320` with the array conversion at `:335` (`fields: fields.map(toFieldPayload)`) — plus its tests, including the landed witness `MetadataService.specKeyObjectPayload.test.ts`.

Non-overlap: **#6238 merged** (PR #6478), so this file is free rather than contended — this branch takes the delete-door change from `main`. Only two other cards are in flight and neither touches `app-shell/src/services/`: #6464 (`src/views/`, `plugin-detail`, `react`) and #6443 (`src/providers/`).

⛔ **#6480 is deliberately NOT dispatched alongside this.** It is this card's sub-issue and its own filer said it "already owns the correctness of this exact PUT body … its `fields` array-vs-map defect **edits the same expression**". Two devs on one expression is the collision a per-card shadow check cannot see. #6480 stays queued until this lands; whoever picks it up then takes the post-fix shape.

**#6481 was considered for this slot and is now `pm:blocked`** behind decision card #6482 — its fix shape is pending a maintainer, and dispatching it today would have been a coin flip on writing a fifth hand copy. Recorded here only so the sequencing is legible: this card was not chosen over a Bug arbitrarily.

Triage's three constraints carry as **dispatch constraints, not options**: the map key must come from a **required** name (a missing name fails loudly, never a `{ undefined: … }` entry); `saveFields`' unknown-server-key preservation must survive the conversion and gains a pin; and the public `existingFields` signature change is **severable** — payload shape first, signature as its own judgement.

And the first step is the card's own unmeasured premise: reproduce what the route actually does with the array today, so the user-visible claim is measured rather than argued.

**ACCEPT** — PR #6491, head `c9a2d916f`. Verified against the tree.

### Step one changed the card's severity, which is what measure-first is for

The card asked what the route does with the array. The answer is **REFUSE, with no category split**: `saveMetaItem` binds metadata type `object` to that same `ObjectSchema`, `safeParse`s the whole item, and throws **422 before persisting**. So the array was not stripped and not stored — **every designer object save and every designer field save through this service was a 422 that wrote nothing**.

That is a materially larger claim than the card made, and it is measured rather than argued: array (populated *or* empty) → `invalid_type @ fields`; map (populated *or* `{}`) → success; key absent → `invalid_type` (required); camelCase key → `invalid_key`.

### ⭐⭐ Trap 1 was honoured with a measurement that **inverts** my reasoning

I wrote the required-name constraint as "a `{ undefined: … }` entry is silently corrupt, worse than the array." The dev checked instead of accepting it, and the check flips the argument's basis:

> `fields: { undefined: ... }` **PARSES GREEN** on 17.2.0.

The spec cannot catch a nameless field at all. So blind keying would have traded **a loud, harmless 422** for **a silently corrupt stored document** — the guard matters *more* than my phrasing implied, and for a reason my phrasing did not contain. `toFieldsMap` throws on a missing or blank name, and the pins assert both the throw **and that no request was issued**.

### Two silent losses the conversion would have introduced — refused, and one is a genuinely sharp catch

- **Duplicate names.** An array can carry two `amount` entries; a map cannot. Converting blind would have dropped one.
- **`__proto__`.** It is a **spec-legal** field name under the record's `/^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$/` key rule, and plain assignment into an object literal invokes the prototype setter and silently drops it. The fix builds with `Object.fromEntries` (`:244`), with the rationale written at `:211-217` where the next reader will meet it.

Neither hazard is in the card. Both are properties of the *conversion itself*, found by thinking about the fix rather than the defect.

### The thing deliberately NOT done is the most valuable judgement here

`saveObject` with no `existingFields` still **omits** the key rather than defaulting to `{}`. Because `{}` parses green and **a PUT is an upsert**, defaulting would have deleted every field of an object on a save that only meant to rename it. That is silent, total data loss on a routine action — introduced by a change whose whole purpose was correctness.

It is pinned as a positive control and **proved load-bearing by ablation D**: injecting the `?? []` default reds exactly one cell, `omits fields entirely … does NOT write {}`, with 73 green.

### Trap 3 severed, and the Clause-② analysis is the best this seat has seen

The signature is **byte-for-byte identical** — I diffed it, only the line number moved (`:275` → `:382`). The conversion happens inside, so the PR is additive-only at the public surface.

And the reachability argument goes a level deeper than the rule I have been applying: `saveObject` **is** reachable from the entry, not because the class or the payload types are re-exported by name, but because `dist/index.d.ts` exports `useMetadataService(): MetadataService | null` — **so the class's method signatures are public through the return type of an exported function**. Checked on the *built* entry, with the observation that it carries zero `export *` chains. The reshaped `ObjectMetadataPayload.fields` appears in no exported signature and has no importer, so its shape growth is not reachable either.

Reachability runs through return types, not just export lists. That belongs in the standing rule.

### Four ablations, each isolating one cell family

A (both writers emit an array again) → 16 cells red including the landed witness, **all five schema-only "instrument" cases and all four sibling pin files green**. B (missing-name guard removed) → exactly the 4 nameless cells red, duplicate/`__proto__`/shape cells green. C (`Object.fromEntries` → assignment) → exactly 1 red, the `__proto__` case. D above → exactly 1 red.

C and D are what make those two cells non-degenerate: each sits precisely where the two readings disagree.

**And the coverage split is stated rather than assumed**: `check:designer-field-key-parity` compares key *names* and `fields` is in the accept set under either shape, so it is green before and after and **is not evidence about this fix** — its own coverage note 4 says so. The half it cannot see is covered by runtime assertions that read `JSON.parse` of the captured PUT body, each with a falsification control beside it.

`check:readme-exports` was correctly classified **NOT MEASURED** rather than red, with proof of the classification: building `app-shell` cleared all 8 of its own findings and left the other six packages' untouched.

---

## Ruling on the two open questions

**Q1 — the severed signature.** **A stands for this PR**, as landed and as the dispatch asked. For **#6490** I am not pre-ruling C: both B (make the argument required) and C (fetch-and-merge, which makes the parameter redundant and then wants retiring) end at a **published signature change**, which is the human floor, not this seat's. Your argument for C over B is the right *input* to that card — no in-repo caller passes `existingFields` today, so B's breakage population is entirely external, and `saveFields` already proves fetch-and-merge works against this same document. Put it on #6490 in those words; the decision belongs there.

**Q2 — `skip-changeset`.** You are right that the label exists and right to ask for B rather than assume. I settled it: **zero workflows read it**, and the repo already has a gate asserting it never will — `scripts/__tests__/ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts:235`, *"never wires the phantom `skip-changeset` label into a workflow or a gate"*, with `:217` recording it as a phantom left behind by objectui#4912.

So the accurate instruction is neither "it does not exist" nor "it is a real mechanism": **it exists as a label object, seven merged PRs carry it, no workflow reads it, and a gate keeps it that way.** This seat's own standing text already says that; the stale version lives in the dev-seat guidance, which is `domain:skills` territory and not mine to edit — recorded here so whoever holds that lane has the measurement.
